data.name: Nivan
data.gender_notes: Nivan is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Nivan is a Sanskrit name derived from the word 'niv' which means 'to conquer' or 'to gain victory over'. It is a name of great significance in Hindu mythology, given to a child born into a victorious family or as a symbol of triumph over adversity. The name is also associated with the god Vishnu, who is believed to grant victory and protect his devotees.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of triumph over adversity, victory in spiritual pursuits
data.etymology: Nivan belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Victory, Triumph.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Nivan total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

data.cultural_impact: Nivan is a Hindi name that carries the symbolism of victory, strength, and triumph. It is a name that resonates with pride and courage, often attributed to those who have achieved something significant, whether in their personal lives or on a grander scale. In Indian culture, it is believed that a child's name holds great power and can influence their destiny, so the name Nivan would be given to a child born into a victorious family or to symbolize a parent's hope for their child's success and triumph over obstacles in life.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Nivan is associated with the god Vishnu, who is believed to bestow victory and protect his devotees. The name signifies the victory of good over evil, the triumph of the spirit over the physical world. It is a reminder of the power of the divine and encourages one to have faith and trust in the universe to guide them through life's challenges. The name Nivan also embodies the concept of reaching the ultimate goal or fulfillment, both in the spiritual and material realm, giving the bearer a sense of purpose and direction in their journey through life.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Nivan signifies the ultimate goal of human life - attaining Moksha, or liberation from the cycle of birth and death. It is a reminder of the eternal journey towards self-realization and union with the Divine.
